denomProfiles/plymouth-brethren/tagline: Assemblies gathering simply to break bread, without clergy, awaiting Christ's return.
denomProfiles/plymouth-brethren/coreDoct: Scripture as the sole and sufficient guide for faith and church order.
The priesthood of all believers, rejecting a separate ordained clergy.
The church as a heavenly body distinct from Israel, within a dispensational scheme.
A pre-tribulation rapture of the church, popularised by J. N. Darby.
denomProfiles/plymouth-brethren/focuses/: Weekly remembrance of the Lord at the breaking of bread.
Separation from worldliness and from denominational systems.
denomProfiles/plymouth-brethren/practice: A Sunday morning "breaking of bread" with open participation by brothers as led by the Spirit.
Leadership by recognised elders rather than paid pastors.
Women typically keep silence in meetings and wear head coverings.
denomProfiles/plymouth-brethren/influenc: Darby's system spread through the Scofield Reference Bible (1909).
Watchman Nee drew heavily on Brethren writers.
Brethren writers and missionaries shaped evangelical Bible teaching and missions.
denomProfiles/plymouth-brethren/keyFigur: Leading teacher and systematiser of dispensationalism.
Early leader and pioneer missionary to Baghdad and India.
Bristol leader and founder of orphanages.
denomProfiles/plymouth-brethren/inIndia: Anthony Norris Groves came to India in 1833, and Brethren assemblies grew in the Godavari delta of Andhra Pradesh and, from the late nineteenth century, in Kerala, which now has one of the largest Brethren communities in the world.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/tagline: Independent Brethren assemblies, led by elders, known for missions and Bible teaching.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/coreDoctrine: The Bible as the inspired, sole authority for doctrine and church order.
Each local assembly is autonomous, under Christ and its elders.
Priesthood of all believers, without ordained clergy.
Generally premillennial and often dispensational eschatology.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/focuses/0: World mission through "faith missions", supported via Echoes of Service (founded 1872).
denomProfiles/open-brethren/focuses/3: Reception of believers on the basis of personal faith rather than association.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/practices/0: Weekly breaking of bread with open participation by men.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/practices/1: Elders and deacons chosen from within, usually unpaid.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/practices/2: Gospel halls and, increasingly, evangelical-style churches.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/practices/3: Missionaries sent out commended by their home assemblies.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/influenced/0: A large indigenous Brethren movement grew in Kerala from the 1890s.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/influenced/1: F. F. Bruce, an Open Brethren layman, shaped evangelical biblical studies.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/influenced/2: The Müller-Groves model informed later faith missions such as the China Inland Mission.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/keyFigures/0: Leader at Bethesda, Bristol, and founder of orphan homes.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/keyFigures/2: Pioneer of the Brethren mission model.
denomProfiles/open-brethren/inIndia: Open Brethren assemblies are numerous in Kerala (with centres such as Kumbanad) and in Andhra Pradesh, a legacy of Groves and of Kerala evangelists from the 1890s onwards.
denomProfiles/exclusive-brethren/tagline: Darbyite Brethren who unite assemblies in one fellowship and practise strict separation.
denomProfiles/exclusive-brethren/coreDoc: The unity of the Spirit expressed in a single connexion of assemblies whose disciplinary decisions bind all.
Separation from evil (2 Timothy 2:19–22) as a principle of fellowship.
Dispensational teaching, including the rapture of the church, following Darby.
Ministry recognised through leading brothers rather than ordained clergy.
denomProfiles/exclusive-brethren/focuses: Purity of fellowship and the Lord's Supper.
Close study of the ministry of recognised teachers.
Separation from the world, which in the Raven–Taylor line includes not eating with outsiders (from 1960).
Family and community life within the fellowship.
denomProfiles/exclusive-brethren/practic: Weekly Lord's Supper restricted to those in fellowship.
Household baptism of believers' children in many Exclusive groups.
In the Plymouth Brethren Christian Church, no television, radio or university residence, and a single "Universal Leader".
Discipline by "withdrawal" from those judged to be in error.
denomProfiles/exclusive-brethren/influen: Watchman Nee was briefly in fellowship with the London (Taylor) Brethren in the 1930s.
Darby's writings spread dispensational teaching worldwide.
denomProfiles/exclusive-brethren/keyFigu: Editor of Darby's works; led a separate group after 1881.
Leader from 1959 who introduced strict separation rules.
Leader of the Plymouth Brethren Christian Church since 2002.
denomProfiles/evangelical-free-church/ta: Scandinavian Pietist free churches: in essentials unity, in non-essentials liberty.
denomProfiles/evangelical-free-church/co: The Bible as the inerrant Word of God.
Salvation by grace through faith in Christ alone.
A short Statement of Faith (1950, revised 2008) focused on gospel essentials.
The personal, premillennial return of Christ.
denomProfiles/evangelical-free-church/fo: Majoring on the essentials of the gospel while allowing liberty elsewhere.
Theological education through Trinity Evangelical Divinity School.
denomProfiles/evangelical-free-church/pr: Congregational autonomy within a national association.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper as ordinances; both believer's and infant baptism have historically been accepted.
Credentialing of pastors, reserved for men since 2023.
denomProfiles/evangelical-free-church/in: A major centre of evangelical scholarship.
Fredrik Franson, a Free Church revivalist, founded TEAM in 1890.
denomProfiles/evangelical-free-church/ke: First president of the merged EFCA (1950).
Dean who built Trinity Evangelical Divinity School.
denomProfiles/evangelical-covenant-churc: Swedish Pietist covenant church asking "Where is it written?" and holding freedom in Christ.
The Bible as the only perfect rule for faith, doctrine and conduct.
The necessity of new birth and a living, personal faith.
A commitment to the whole mission of the church: evangelism and compassion.
Freedom in Christ on disputed matters such as the mode of baptism.
Spiritual renewal in the Pietist tradition.
Church planting and multi-ethnic congregations.
Mercy, justice and global mission.
Higher education through North Park University and Seminary in Chicago.
Both infant baptism and believer's baptism, by conscience of the parents or candidate.
Baptism and the Lord's Supper honoured as sacraments.
Congregational polity within a covenanting denomination.
Ordination of women, since 1976.
Multi-ethnic church planting
Its church-planting programmes have shaped American evangelical practice.
Covenant churches worldwide
Partner Covenant churches exist in Africa, Asia and Latin America through the International Federation of Free Evangelical Churches.
Paul Peter Waldenström
Swedish theologian of the Mission Covenant.
Carl August Björk
First president of the American Covenant (1885).
David Nyvall
First president of North Park College.
denomProfiles/christian-and-missionary-a: A. B. Simpson's missionary fellowship preaching the Fourfold Gospel.
The Fourfold Gospel: Jesus Christ as Saviour, Sanctifier, Healer and Coming King.
Sanctification as a crisis of surrender followed by progressive growth (Keswick-influenced).
Divine healing provided in the atonement.
The premillennial return of Christ, linked to completing world evangelisation.
Pioneer world missions among unreached peoples.
The deeper or "victorious" Christian life.
Prayer for the sick.
Theological training (Nyack College, founded 1882).
Believer's baptism by immersion and the Lord's Supper as ordinances.
Anointing with oil and prayer for healing.
Openness to spiritual gifts under the principle "seek not, forbid not".
Annual missions conventions and giving to the Great Commission Fund.
Assemblies of God
Many early Assemblies of God leaders and much of its doctrinal language came from the Alliance.
Pentecostalism
The Alliance's healing and Spirit teaching fed early Pentecostalism.
A. W. Tozer's writings
Tozer's devotional classics reached readers far beyond the Alliance.
A. B. Simpson
Founder (1887) and hymn writer.
A. W. Tozer
Pastor and author of The Pursuit of God (1948).
Robert A. Jaffray
Pioneer of Alliance missions in China and Indonesia.
Alliance missionaries began work in Berar and Khandesh (today's Maharashtra and Gujarat) in the 1890s, giving rise to the Christian and Missionary Alliance churches of western India.
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/tagline: Jesus Movement fellowship of verse-by-verse Bible teaching and relaxed worship.
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/coreDoctrin: The Bible as the inerrant Word of God, taught systematically.
Salvation by grace through faith; a balance between Calvinism and Arminianism.
The gifts of the Spirit are for today, exercised decently and in order.
A pre-tribulation rapture and premillennial return of Christ.
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/focuses/0: Expository teaching through whole books of the Bible.
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/focuses/2: Worship music, pioneered by Maranatha! Music (1971).
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/practices/1: Believer's baptism, often in the ocean.
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/practices/2: Pastor-led governance, called the "Moses model", with church boards in support.
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/practices/3: Afterglow prayer meetings for those seeking spiritual gifts.
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/influenced/: John Wimber's churches began within Calvary Chapel before separating in 1982.
Maranatha! Music helped create the praise-and-worship genre.
Greg Laurie's church and crusades grew from Calvary Chapel.
denomProfiles/calvary-chapel/keyFigures/: Founding pastor of Calvary Chapel Costa Mesa (1965).
Pastor and evangelist of Harvest Christian Fellowship.
denomProfiles/grace-communion-internatio: Former Worldwide Church of God, transformed into a Trinitarian evangelical church.
The Trinity, embraced in the 1990s after its earlier denial.
Salvation by grace through faith, not by keeping Old Testament laws.
A Trinitarian, incarnational theology influenced by T. F. and J. B. Torrance.
The New Covenant fulfils the Sabbath and festivals, which are no longer required.
Grace and the life of the Trinity.
Pastoral care through a reformed denomination.
Theological education through Grace Communion Seminary.
Reconciliation after a painful doctrinal transition.
Sunday worship (Saturday is permitted), after decades of Sabbath-only observance.
Believer's baptism and the Lord's Supper.
Ordination of women as elders, since 2007.
Membership of the National Association of Evangelicals (since 1997).
Armstrongite splinter churches
Members who rejected the reforms formed United Church of God, Philadelphia Church of God and others.
Studies of cult renewal
Its transformation is widely cited as a rare case of a whole movement moving to orthodoxy.
Herbert W. Armstrong
Founder of the parent Radio/Worldwide Church of God (1934).
Joseph W. Tkach
Pastor general (1986–1995) who led the reforms.
Joseph Tkach Jr
Leader who completed the transition and renaming.
Thomas F. Torrance
Theological influence.
denomProfiles/messianic-judaism/tagline: Jewish believers in Yeshua as Messiah who keep Jewish identity and practice.
denomProfiles/messianic-judaism/coreDoct: Yeshua (Jesus) is the promised Messiah of Israel and Lord.
Jewish followers of Yeshua remain Jews; their covenant identity continues.
The Hebrew Bible and the New Covenant Scriptures are inspired.
Most affirm the divinity of Messiah and the Trinity, often in Jewish idiom.
denomProfiles/messianic-judaism/focuses/: Bilateral ecclesiology: Jewish and Gentile believers as distinct parts of one body (Kinzer).
Love for Israel and the Jewish people.
denomProfiles/messianic-judaism/practice: Shabbat services, often on Friday evening or Saturday, with Hebrew liturgy and Torah reading.
Observance of biblical festivals, especially Passover seders that point to Messiah.
Kosher observance and circumcision in many congregations.
denomProfiles/messianic-judaism/influenc: Founded by Moishe Rosen (1973) as an evangelistic mission.
Messianic theologians contribute to post-supersessionist Christian thought.
denomProfiles/messianic-judaism/keyFigur: Pioneer of a Jewish-Christian congregation in Kishinev.
Translator of the Complete Jewish Bible.
